correctness.rationale: The positive J_{3/2} roots are exactly the nonzero positive tan x=x roots, one per stated interval by strict increase and the endpoint signs. For β=β_n and u=(n+1/2)π−β=arctan(1/β), the square defect d=2βu+u² satisfies d>2 by u cot u>1−u²/2, and d<2+π⁻² since u<1/β<1/π. In the three-square relation the integer odd-square combination N is 1 mod 8, while the combined defect is strictly between 2−π⁻² and 2+2π⁻². This gives the strict Δ margin for N≥1 and a stronger one for N≤−7, also with repeated indices. Δ>0 as follows already from π>3.1. For positive roots a,b, exact sine/cosine addition gives sin(a+b)≠0 and cot(a+b)=(1−ab)/(a+b); fixed sum thus fixes the product, giving the unordered pair, and a+b cannot be a root because it would require ab=0. Radial integration of the unit-ball indicator gives 4π(sin q−q cos q)/q³ for q=2π|ξ|>0. Hence polarity at each vertex divides the squared-zero expression by 8π², and collinearity would force an excluded sum of two roots. The frozen script is only a finite floating-point check (30 roots, 27,000 ordered squared triples and 4,096 ordered sum quadruples); it was inspected, not executed. The result is established by the exact proof.
